scope: Three-interval synthetic integer-quantized electrical schedule. Interval 1 has one PV quantum and zero load; interval 2 is a grid outage with one essential quantum demanded; interval 3 has one essential quantum demanded and grid import at 5 cost units and 100 carbon grams per quantum. The one-quantum idealized battery can carry PV energy forward. These objective factors are synthetic test constants, not real tariff or emissions data.
derivation: The 9 feasible complete schedules are the feasible branches over interval-1 PV curtail/charge; interval-2 outage service using the stored quantum or leaving demand unserved; and interval-3 grid service, battery discharge, charge-from-grid or unserved service, under the one-quantum battery capacity and no simultaneous charge/discharge rule. The full non-dominated objective set retains the trade-offs between essential shortfall, synthetic grid cost/carbon and terminal SOC. Frontier order is essential unserved, flexible unserved, cost, carbon, curtailment ascending, then terminal SOC descending.
